name: NC-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Deborah Ross running with a large cash advantage
Republican challenger has raised essentially nothing
Prediction markets price Ross near certain to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Ross: a D+17 district, incumbency, and a roughly $1.7 million warhead of fundraising against a Republican with no reported money. Polymarket prices her win probability at about 94%, and no polls or expert ratings suggest any reason to move away from the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing the challenger within single digits, or major outside spending against Ross, would be the first sign this safe seat is in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Deborah Ross, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Raleigh-area district that leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 17 points. She enters the general election with a substantial financial edge, having raised roughly $1.7 million and holding more than $1.3 million on hand, while her Republican opponent, Eugene Douglass, reports no fundraising activity. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but is not considered a significant factor.

No public polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price Ross as an overwhelming favorite. The expected margin is in the low-to-mid twenties, with Ross highly likely to win re-election.
